({{IPA|es|ˈraʝo βaʎeˈkano ðe maˈðɾið}}),{{efn|In isolation, ''Vallecano'' is pronounced {{IPA|es|baʎeˈkano|}}.}} often abbreviated to '''Rayo''' (Spanish for "lightning bolt"), is a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in the [[Puente de Vallecas]] district of [[Madrid]], Spain. The club competes in [[La Liga]], the top flight of [[Spanish football league system|Spanish football]]. Founded on 29 May 1924, the club is known for its sociocultural tradition, recognized for representing the [[barrio]]-local culture and its [[Working class|working-class]] status. Its home matches have been played at the 14,708-capacity [[Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas]] stadium since 1976.{{Cite web|url=http://www.rayovallecano.es/club/estadio|title=Estadio de Vallecas {{!}} Rayo - Web Oficial|website=Estadio de Vallecas {{!}} Rayo - Web Oficial|language=es|access-date=2020-01-18|archive-date=2017-07-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708210040/http://www.rayovallecano.es/club/estadio|url-status=live}} [[File:Panoramica estadio de vallecas.jpg|right|310px|thumb|Rayo Vallecano home stadium Vallecas.]] During its history, Rayo has spent 22 seasons in the top-flight, and has played in two European competitions, the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] in the [[2000–01 UEFA Cup|2000–01 season]] and the [[2025–26 UEFA Conference League]]. The club won the [[2017–18 Segunda División]]. By historical performance, Rayo is the third best club in Community of Madrid, after [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Atlético Madrid]]. ==History== ===Establishment and early years=== Rayo Vallecano was founded on 29 May 1924 in the hometown of Prudencia Priego, wife of the club's first president Julián Huerta. Greatly inspired by [[Argentina]]'s [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]], in 1949, after an agreement with [[Atlético Madrid]], a red diagonal stripe was added to the team's kit, and the club reached [[Tercera División]] for the first time in its history.{{cite web|url=http://www.rayovallecano.es/historia/|title=Historia resumida del Rayo|trans-title=Brief history of Rayo|publisher=Rayo Vallecano|language=es|access-date=4 April 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407061142/http://www.rayovallecano.es/historia/|archive-date=7 April 2014}} ===Yo-yo years=== One of the perennial [[Yo-yo club|yo-yo clubs]] of Spanish football, and always in the shadow of the two biggest clubs in the city ([[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] and [[Atlético Madrid]]), Rayo Vallecano spent many years during the 1980s and 1990s moving back and forth between [[La Liga]] and [[Segunda División]]. The 1983–84 season was the worst during the 1980s. The club finished in the last position in Segunda División and was relegated to Segunda División B.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/t/t1983-842a.html|title=Classification 2nd Division 1983-84|website=www.bdfutbol.com|access-date=2019-11-05|archive-date=2019-04-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425053214/https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/t/t1983-842a.html|url-status=live}} Due to a tragedy Rayo Vallecano turned out to be [[Laurie Cunningham]]'s last club; he was killed in a car crash just outside Madrid in 1989, after a sole season. He had recently won an [[F.A. Cup]] winners medal with [[Wimbledon F.C.]] in England the previous year and had also represented neighbours Real Madrid for four years. They appeared to have consolidated their top flight status after [[1998–99 Segunda División|gaining promotion in 1999]], and the team's most successful season came in [[2000–01 La Liga|2000–01]] when they [[2000–01 UEFA Cup|reached the quarter-finals]] of the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]], going out only to eventual runners-up [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]];{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/uefa_cup/1220513.stm|title=Alaves through as Rayo fall|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=15 March 2001|access-date=4 April 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407101012/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/uefa_cup/1220513.stm|archive-date=7 April 2014}} Rayo finished ninth in [[1999–2000 La Liga|the previous campaign]], but entered the competition via the [[UEFA Fair Play ranking|fair play draw]].{{cite web|url=http://deportes.terra.es/valladolid/el-fair-play-una-puerta-abierta-para-jugar-en-europa,df54797edf78d310VgnVCM3000009acceb0aRCRD.html|title=El 'Fair Play', ¿una puerta abierta para jugar en Europa?|trans-title='Fair Play', open door to play in Europe?|publisher=Terra|language=es|date=20 March 2013|access-date=4 April 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407101328/http://deportes.terra.es/valladolid/el-fair-play-una-puerta-abierta-para-jugar-en-europa,df54797edf78d310VgnVCM3000009acceb0aRCRD.html|archive-date=7 April 2014}} ===2003–11: Segunda División and below=== [[File:Deportivorayo.JPG|thumb|320px|[[Deportivo de La Coruña]] vs. Rayo Vallecano]] However, the club shortly thereafter fell on hard times, enduring successive relegations in [[2002–03 La Liga|2003]] and [[2003–04 Segunda División|2004]]. Affiliate of [[Atlético Madrid]] in 1949–50 ==Club culture and supporters== Rayo Vallecano is a football club based in the [[Vallecas]] neighbourhood of Madrid, traditionally considered a working-class area with a strong leftist identity. Vallecas was a [[Republican faction (Spanish Civil War)|Republican]] stronghold during the [[Spanish Civil War]] and grew significantly under the [[Francisco Franco|Franco]] regime as it received migrants from other parts of Spain, many of whom had experienced economic hardship or political repression.{{cite news |last=Seymour |first=Dylan |date=21 October 2024 |title=The ultras groups fighting back against fascism in football |url=https://www.thecourieronline.co.uk/the-ultras-groups-fighting-back-against-fascism-in-football/ |work=[[The Courier (Newcastle University newspaper)|The Courier]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}} The club is closely associated with the local community, and both the neighbourhood and the club maintain a distinct identity, often emphasised through the alternative spelling "Vallekas".{{cite news |last=McGill |first=Stewart |date= 31 May 2020 |title=Hermanos de la Izquierda - Brothers on the left |url=https://morningstaronline.co.uk/article/s/hermanos-de-la-izquierda-brothers-left |work=[[Morning Star (British newspaper)|Morning Star]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}}{{cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=8 February 2022 |title=Rayo Vallecano have never been better, but divide between owner and fans has never been greater |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37625201/rayo-vallecano-never-better-divide-owner-fans-never-greater |work=[[ESPN]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}} Consequently, Rayo Vallecano’s supporters, particularly the ultras group Bukaneros, are often left-wing, anti-fascist, and politically active. In the stands, they regularly display banners, flags, and visual displays expressing opposition to racism, fascism, homophobia, and the commercialisation of football, while also supporting women's rights, workers' rights, and international solidarity, including pro-Palestine messaging. Chants often carry political content, and fans have a tradition of imaginative collective protest, such as mocking league decisions on match scheduling or highlighting perceived exploitation of supporters. Republican flags, [[Che Guevara]] images, and the Spanish Civil War slogan "¡[[No pasarán]]!" are commonly displayed at games.{{cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=27 November 2014 |title=Rayo Vallecano demonstrate why they're different from the rest |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37407649/rayo-vallecano-demonstrate-why-different-rest |work=[[ESPN]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}} In 2014 the club and fan base aided Carmen Martinez Ayudo, an 85-year-old local woman, after she was evicted from her home, and flew banners reading "The evictions of a sick state, the solidarity of a working-class neighbourhood" displayed at the following match.{{cite news |last=Glendenning |first=Barry |date=6 November 2015 |title=The Joy of Six: hipsters' favourite football clubs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2015/nov/06/the-joy-of-six-hipsters-favourite-football-clubs |work=[[The Guardian]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}} In late March 2012, the Rayo squad took one day off training to join demonstrations supporting the [[2011–12 Spanish protests]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wsc.co.uk/content/view/8471/38/|title=Rayo Vallecano players strike over Spanish austerity cuts|publisher=When Saturday Comes|date=29 March 2012|access-date=30 March 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331180800/http://www.wsc.co.uk/content/view/8471/38|archive-date=31 March 2012}} The fanbase actively enforces its political views; In February 2017, Ukrainian player [[Roman Zozulya]] left the club after one training session due to chants by Rayo fans accusing him of far-right affiliations; Zozulya denied any such associations and returned to his parent club Real Betis.{{Cite news |date=2019-12-15 |title=Rayo Vallecano match abandoned after 'Nazi' chants; Real Madrid draw |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/15/spanish-football-nazi-chants-roman-zozulya-rayo-vallecano-albacete-valencia-real-madrid |access-date=2023-02-10 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=2023-02-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210014950/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/15/spanish-football-nazi-chants-roman-zozulya-rayo-vallecano-albacete-valencia-real-madrid |url-status=live }}{{cite news |last=Perez |first=Gorka |date=6 February 2017 |title=Caso Zozulya: “¡Esta es la grada antifascista!” |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/02/05/actualidad/1486305594_185016.html |work= |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026 |language=es}} Following the training ground incident, Rayo Vallecano fans continued to target Roman Zozulya in December 2019 during a Segunda División match against [[Albacete Balompié]], whom Zozulya eventually moved to. The match was abandoned at half-time after home supporters chanted "Zozulya, you are a Nazi!". The league, both clubs, and the referee agreed to suspend the game to protect players and uphold competition values. Rayo's president, Raúl Martín Presa, publicly condemned the chants and met with Zozulya to express support and respect.{{cite news |last= |first= |date=15 December 2019 |title=Rayo Vallecano match abandoned after ‘Nazi’ chants; Real Madrid draw |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/15/spanish-football-nazi-chants-roman-zozulya-rayo-vallecano-albacete-valencia-real-madrid |work=[[The Guardian]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}} Supporters of the club have come into conflict with clubs of opposing ideologies: Rayo Vallecano fans have violently clashed with right-wing nationalist supporters, including Polish clubs [[Jagiellonia Białystok]] and [[Lech Poznań]], during encounters that both occurred in 2025.{{cite news |last=Carter |first=Jon |date=11 December 2025 |title=Masked football fans ambush Spanish rivals in eastern Poland |url=https://tvpworld.com/90494728/seven-polish-football-hooligans-detained-after-attack-on-spanish-rivals |work=[[TVP World]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026}}{{cite news |last=Rodríguez |first=Ángel |date=6 November 2025 |title=Guerra ultra en Vallecas: "Quedada" entre Bukaneros y radicales del Lech Poznan tras el 'asalto' al estadio |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/conference-league/2025/11/06/guerra-ultra-vallecas-quedada-bukaneros-radicales-lech-poznan-asalto-estadio.html |work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026 |language=es}} In September 2025, members of the Bukaneros were reported to have acted as part of a security detail escorting [[Podemos (Spanish political party)|Podemos]] leaders [[Ione Belarra]] and [[Irene Montero]] during pro-Palestinian protests at the end of a stage of [[Vuelta a España]] in Madrid. The group was coordinated by lawyer Erlantz Ibarrondo, a long-standing figure on the Spanish radical left, and included other Bukaneros supporters. The protests involved clashes with police, with 22 officers injured and two people arrested, and led to the suspension of the stage finish and award ceremony in Plaza de Cibeles. The Bukaneros and legal team were present to prevent the political leaders from being crowded or attacked by other demonstrators.{{cite news |last=Sánchez |first=Jose |date=16 September 2025 |title=Ultras de Bukaneros y un abogado de la extrema izquierda escoltaron a Belarra y Montero en las protestas de La Vuelta |url=https://www.vozpopuli.com/sucesos/montero-y-belarra-usaron-la-escolta-de-interior-durante-las-violentas-protestas-de-la-vuelta.html |work=Voz Populi |location= |publisher= |access-date=6 January 2026 |language=es}} [[File:Alineación Rayo Vallecano1.jpg|thumb|upright=1|Kits featuring [[Rainbow flag (LGBTQ)|rainbow symbolism]] used by Rayo Vallecano in 2015/2016 to represent various causes. Los Bukaneros criticised the concept on the basis that they did not believe the management at the club was doing enough to support those causes.]] The fanbase is independent and frequently opposes the club's management. Rayo Vallecano's fans do not have a good relationship with the current owner [[Raúl Martín Presa]] and regularly chant for him to leave.{{Cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=2021-12-20 |title=Rayo Vallecano: a mess, 'problem after problem' … and top four in La Liga |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/20/rayo-vallecano-mess-problem-top-four-la-liga |access-date=2023-02-11 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=2023-02-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230211001222/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/20/rayo-vallecano-mess-problem-top-four-la-liga |url-status=live }}{{Cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=2021-09-20 |title=The Tiger who came for free: Falcao is back and scoring in La Liga |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2021/sep/20/the-tiger-who-came-for-free-radamel-falcao-is-back-and-scoring-in-la-liga-rayo-vallecano |access-date=2023-02-11 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=2023-02-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230211001223/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2021/sep/20/the-tiger-who-came-for-free-radamel-falcao-is-back-and-scoring-in-la-liga-rayo-vallecano |url-status=live }} In July 2015, Rayo Vallecano unveiled a new kit featuring a rainbow, with each colour representing a different social cause: red for those fighting cancer, orange for disability integration, yellow for hope, green for environmental protection, blue against child abuse, indigo against domestic abuse, and violet for LGBTQ+ equality. Part of the proceeds from kit sales were pledged to these causes. Opened on 10 May 1976, at first it was called "New Stadium Vallecas", but in January 2004, 13 years after the arrival of the Ruiz-Mateos family in 1991, it changed denominations, as the wife was also named by her husband, businessman [[José María Ruiz Mateos|José María]], the first woman president of an elite football team. It has a capacity of 14,708 spectators in an all-seated format and dimensions of 100×67 m. after the enlargement of the width and the reduction of the length of the pitch after the remodelling of the grandstands, compulsory due to the elimination of the fences surrounding the pitch. The pitch is one the smallest in La Liga.
